plugin.name: Magpie
plugin.description: Connect the magpie gateway running on this computer to Astravia: read its model catalog, publish it as a model provider, and use any of those models in chat.
view.label: Magpie Gateway
view.description: Models served by the magpie gateway on this computer
settings.title: Connection
settings.baseUrlHint: Leave it alone unless magpie was started with a different MAGPIE_ADDR.
settings.apiKeyHint: Only needed when magpie was started outside this computer. Anything works from this computer, so the default stays as it is.
models.title: Models on this gateway
models.empty: The gateway answered with an empty catalog. Add a provider in magpie first.
setup.title: Nothing is listening on {{endpoint}}
setup.body: This plugin talks to a magpie gateway that is already installed. Start magpie (the menu-bar app, the window, or `magpie serve` in a terminal) and check again — the gateway listens on 127.0.0.1:3425 by default.
setup.installHint: Download it from usemagpie.ai, or run:
note.title: What this plugin does not do
note.body: It does not install, start or stop magpie, and it does not hold your provider keys — those stay in magpie's own configuration on this computer. It reads the gateway's catalog and, when you ask it to, writes those models into Astravia's model picker.
error.unreachable: No answer from the gateway; is magpie running?
error.timeout: The gateway took too long to answer
error.notMagpie: Something answered at that address, but not a magpie gateway
error.http: The gateway answered with an error
error.syncFailed: Could not publish the models; nothing was changed
error.emptyModels: The catalog is empty, so nothing was written to Astravia
